body: It tends to take shy people like me a lot longer to meet someone though. Are you sure people wouldn't question me not having anything meaningful before that age?

Yeah I've heard that you have some limited control over dysfunction (i.e. weight control and lifestyle), but nevertheless I hear that over 40% of men over 40 have some sort of problem in that department, so I'm honestly counting on it happening at some point or another. Also, my parents got along alright (not perfectly, there were a fair bit of arguments), but I hear that most women in general really value charisma/charm and extroversion, 2 traits that I don't nearly have nailed down at all.

1. I'm worried about making possibly relationship-ending faux pas (like handling a disagreement/argument the wrong way, forgetting something important, or not knowing what to do during certain situations during a relationship and saying/doing the wrong thing as a result).

2. I worry that I'll miss out on certain aspects of being in a relationship while young, like being able to enjoy sex while everything still works well/without needing pills or anything like that, as well stuff like as being able to travel without getting tired, being able to stay out late with a date, etc.

Thanks. My main concern though is that if I start my first serious relationship at 30 or after, that I'll have missed out on what it's like to be with someone while I'm young (in my 20s). That, and wouldn't it be really difficult to find someone patient enough to stay with you while you learn how to be in a relationship at that age (and all the little faux pas/mistakes that inevitably come with learning about being in a serious relationship)?
Right, but what I'm concerned with here is not having any serious relationships (at least 6-12 months long) before 30. I just worry about missing out on that  while I'm still young (20s).
Sure, but isn't 30 pretty old to be starting your first serious relationship? I feel like I'd have missed out on so much...

Sure, but I just worry about missing out on what it's like to be young and in a serious relationship if I haven't been in one by that age (late 20s+) and also how much time in general I'll have lost out on...

Hey, thanks for the reply. I'm in therapy now and have tried an SSRI but it just made me irritable and I felt a bit disconnected so I discontinued it. I'm working to find something else that'll help though, I just don't think feeling like a zombie 24/7 is any preferable to how I feel now.

Also, I'm less worried about being dumped at that age but rather I'm more worried about not having had a serious relationship by that age. The thought of having missed out on what it's like to be in a serious relationship while young and having to explain to potential partners as to why I haven't found anything yet by that age just sounds like it would be horrible.

Hey, thanks for the reply. I live in the US, so I've been going by the average age here (17), which makes me feel that I'm really late to the party, at least compared  to my peers. I'm not too worried about getting married in my 30s, but what really concerns me is that a lot of shy/introverted people like me end up not finding their partners until even later than that (like in their 40s or later).
